import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Ledger.ChiLedger

/-!
# The χ-ledger's residue weights are trivial over an algebraically closed field

The χ-ledger ported into this project (`RiemannRoch/Ledger/`, 35 files, sorry-free) computes
degrees **weighted by residue degrees**: `CurveDivisor.deg K D = ∑ₓ Dₓ · [κ(x) : K]`
(`Ledger/Divisor.lean`). The `RiemannRoch/WeilDivisor.lean` notion `Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree`
is the **bare** coefficient sum. So the ledger's `deg_divOf` — principal divisors have degree
zero, `Ledger/ChiLedger.lean` — does not immediately give the unweighted statement.

This file closes that mismatch at the binders where it can be closed: over an **algebraically
closed** base field every residue degree is `1`, so the two notions of degree agree. That is
exactly the binder set of `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero`, whose non-constant branch
is the target (it carries `[IsAlgClosed kbar]`), so the weighting is *discharged* rather than
assumed away.

## Why this is not a duplicate of the adelic lemma

This project already has `Adelic.residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve`
(`RiemannRoch/Adelic/ResidueField.lean`). It is about a **different** `residueDeg`: the adelic
one is `Module.finrank k (localStepTgt k P 1)`, a single-point section quotient of the adelic
filtration (`Adelic/ChiLedger.lean:638`), whereas the ledger's is
`Module.finrank K (X.residueField x)`, the honest residue field
(`Ledger/ClosedPoint.lean:128`). Same name, same value on a curve, different definitions and
different files — so the adelic lemma does not apply here and this is not a re-derivation.
It is also cheaper: the ledger's version needs no adelic machinery at all.

## Main results

* `finrank_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_of_ringHom` — the algebra: over an algebraically closed `K`, a
  field `A` receiving a ring hom from `K` and finite as a `K`-module along it has
  `finrank K A = 1`. Stated against a **ring hom** with the module structure passed explicitly,
  because that is the shape the scheme site provides (see below).
* `Scheme.residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed` — over an algebraically closed base field, the
  ledger residue degree at a closed point of a curve is `1`. Combines the algebra with the
  ledger's own `Scheme.residueDeg_finite`, whose hypotheses are exactly the curve binders.

## The instance-shape trap, recorded because it cost the obvious spelling

`X.residueField x` does **not** carry a global `Algebra K` instance. The ledger supplies only
`Scheme.residueFieldOverModule`, a `Module K` structure obtained by restriction of scalars
along the ring hom `Scheme.residueOverAlgebraMap`, and it is deliberately *not* an instance —
`Ledger/ClosedPoint.lean` records the same overlap hazard as `Scheme.overModule`. So the
natural statement `[Field A] [Algebra K A] → finrank K A = 1` cannot be applied at
`X.residueField x`: instance search fails with `failed to synthesize Algebra K ↑(X.residueField x)`.

Nor does adding `[Module K A]` plus a compatibility hypothesis work: one then has two `Module K A`
structures — the assumed one and `Algebra.toModule` of the locally-built algebra — and
`finrank` is stated against whichever Lean synthesises, giving "synthesized type class instance
is not definitionally equal to expression inferred by typing rules".

The spelling that works is to take the ring hom as data and write the module instance
**explicitly** in the statement, `@Module.finrank K A _ _ f.toModule`. Then `letI` of
`f.toAlgebra` inside the proof produces an `Algebra` whose `toModule` is *definitionally*
`f.toModule`, so no transport is needed and the two never have to be reconciled. Same species
of finding as the workspace's standing note that carrier friction here is usually synthesis and
looks like mathematics.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

/-- **Over an algebraically closed field, a finite field extension is trivial** — stated
against a ring hom, with the module structure explicit.

The `@Module.finrank K A _ _ f.toModule` spelling is load-bearing rather than pedantic: the
consumer (`Scheme.residueDeg`) has only a `Module K` obtained by restriction of scalars along a
ring hom, with no `Algebra` instance available, and the `[Algebra K A]` form of this statement
therefore does not apply there. See the module docstring for the two spellings that fail. -/
theorem finrank_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_of_ringHom (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K]
    (A : Type u) [Field A] (f : K →+* A)
    (hfin : @Module.Finite K A _ _ f.toModule) :
    @Module.finrank K A _ _ f.toModule = 1 := by
  letI : Algebra K A := f.toAlgebra
  haveI : Module.Finite K A := hfin
  haveI : Algebra.IsIntegral K A := Algebra.IsIntegral.of_finite K A
  have hb : Function.Bijective (algebraMap K A) :=
    IsAlgClosed.algebraMap_bijective_of_isIntegral
  have e : K ≃ₐ[K] A := AlgEquiv.ofBijective (Algebra.ofId K A) hb
  simpa using (LinearEquiv.finrank_eq e.toLinearEquiv).symm

attribute [local instance] Scheme.residueFieldOverModule

variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]

/-- **The ledger residue degree is `1` over an algebraically closed base field.**

`Scheme.residueDeg K X x = [κ(x) : K]` and over `K = K̄` the residue field at a closed point of
a curve is `K` itself, so the weight is `1`. Consequently the ledger's weighted degree
`CurveDivisor.deg` agrees with a bare coefficient sum at these binders — which is the mismatch
between `Ledger/ChiLedger.deg_divOf` and `Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree` that
`Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero` has to cross, and it carries `[IsAlgClosed]`, so
this discharges the weighting rather than assuming it away.

Both inputs are already present: finiteness of the residue field is the ledger's own
`Scheme.residueDeg_finite`, stated at exactly these curve binders, and the algebra is
`finrank_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_of_ringHom` above. Nothing adelic is used — in particular this
is *not* `Adelic.residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve`, which is about a different
`residueDeg` (see the module docstring). -/
theorem Scheme.residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed [IsAlgClosed K]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) :
    X.residueDeg K x = 1 :=
  finrank_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_of_ringHom K (X.residueField x)
    (X.residueOverAlgebraMap K x) (Scheme.residueDeg_finite (K := K) (X := X) hx)

end AlgebraicGeometry
